n: This is a royal wedding song. The poet’s heart overflows with a beautiful theme, and his tongue moves as fast as a skilled scribe’s pen.
The king is praised as the most handsome of men, with gracious speech. Christians have long read this king as a picture of Christ.

f.w: grace is poured into thy lips

n: The king is called to strap on his sword and appear in splendor as a mighty warrior.
He rides out victoriously for the cause of truth, humility, and righteousness — a king who fights for good things.
His arrows strike the hearts of his enemies, and nations fall before him.
Remarkably, the king is addressed as “God,” whose throne lasts forever. Hebrews quotes these verses about Jesus Christ, the eternal King.

f.w: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever

f.g: A royal staff, the symbol of rule; a “right sceptre” means just rule.

n: Because he loves righteousness, God has anointed him with joy above all others. “Anointed” is the root of Messiah and Christ.

f.w: anointed thee with the oil of gladness

f.g: Your companions — other kings or the bridegroom’s friends.

n: His wedding robes are scented with precious spices, and music from ivory-decorated palaces makes him glad.

f.g: Costly fragrant spices; myrrh and aloes were also used at Jesus’ burial.

n: Princesses are among the honored ladies, and the queen stands at his right hand in the finest gold.

f.g: Ophir was a distant land famous for fine gold.

n: Now the bride is addressed: listen, and leave behind your family and homeland to begin a new life. Many see here a picture of the Church as the bride of Christ, leaving the world behind.
The king will delight in her beauty. Since he is now her lord, she should honor him.

f.g: Bow before him — a gesture of honor to a king.

n: Even wealthy Tyre will bring gifts, and the rich will seek her favor.

f.g: The people of Tyre, a rich Phoenician trading city.

n: The princess is radiant in her chamber, dressed in gold-woven clothing.

f.g: Inside the palace chamber — possibly also a hint of inner beauty.
Woven or embroidered with gold thread.

n: She is led to the king in embroidered robes, followed by her bridesmaids.
The wedding procession enters the palace with joy and celebration.
The poet turns to the king: your sons will take your ancestors’ place and become princes everywhere. Covenant blessings extend to future generations.
The poet promises to make the king’s name remembered in every generation, so that people will praise him forever.
